reasons: Both answers are accurate and closely aligned on the EUR 1 SL, its below-3,000 safeguards, the immigration check and the autonomo comparison; both mention the notary and Registro Mercantil only in passing, as setup costs, rather than stating them as formal requirements. A adds the Art. 62.2 LSC founders' declaration as an alternative to the bank certificate, current Spanish corporate-tax detail (the Ley 7/2024 micro-company rates and the 2025 change to GILTI) and a concrete profit threshold for when an SL pays off, which makes it slightly more useful. B's FBAR/FATCA mention is a useful addition, but its hedged claim that autonomos societarios often cannot get the tarifa plana is doubtful.

B: Suggests autonomos societarios often cannot get the tarifa plana, although case law has recognised their access to it (hedged).
